idiom_name: step coalgebra plus corecursive assembly (unfold / produce-until-stop)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one step function seed -> Stop | Next(element, nextSeed) and one scheme that applies it repeatedly, either assembling a recursive structure or passing each layer to a consumer as it is produced. Termination belongs to the step function or to an explicit fuel parameter; the scheme itself never decides, and a bounded variant is the honest default for input-driven seeds. Make generation demand-driven where the runtime allows it, so the consumer controls how much work happens, and keep the seed immutable so the same unfold can be replayed or shared. When the produced structure is consumed immediately, fuse the two phases instead of materialising it.
code_sketch:
unfold(seed):
    loop:
        step = f(seed)              # coalgebra: Stop | Next(x, next_seed)
        if step is Stop: break
        emit(step.x)                # hand one layer to a sink, or append it
        seed = step.next_seed       # immutable: never mutate the caller's state
# bounded form: unfold(seed, fuel) with fuel decremented per emitted layer
pitfalls: An unbounded step function with neither a stop condition nor fuel: the scheme is total only in the sense that it runs - it never terminates.
Mixing generation with consumption in one function, which reintroduces exactly the coupling the pattern removes.
Mutating the seed in place, so replaying the unfold or sharing the state between producers yields different structures.

Wrong move: holding the head of a memoising lazy unfold (Scala Stream/LazyList caches every realised element) -> the whole produced spine stays reachable and a long walk over an endless unfold ends in OutOfMemoryError -> instead consume through an Iterator or drop the head reference as soon as each prefix is consumed.

Wrong move: encoding termination as a sentinel element inside the emitted layer (a zero, an empty node) that every consumer must filter -> the stop rule leaks out of the step function and one forgetful consumer yields a poisoned structure -> instead return the Stop/None branch of the coalgebra so termination stays in one place.

Wrong move: reading a clock, global or shared RNG inside the step function instead of threading it through the seed -> forcing the same unfold twice produces different structures, so the replayable-producer and property-testability claims silently fail -> make every input the step function depends on part of the seed value.
